message.content:
For outdoor garden sculptures, **granite** and **marble** are the most popular choices: | Rock | Pros | Cons | |------|------|------| | **Granite** | • Extremely durable, weather‑resistant, and resistant to erosion.
• Holds fine detail well when carved.
• Available in many colors (black, white, pink, green). | • Heavier than other stones – requires sturdy foundations.
• Can be more expensive depending on source. | | **Marble** | • Classic aesthetic; smooth finish with subtle veining.
• Carves easily, allowing intricate designs.
• Translucent quality gives a timeless look. | • Softer than granite – can chip or crack under heavy impact.
• Susceptible to acid rain (alkaline stone reacts with acidic pollutants). | | **Limestone** | • Easier to carve, good for detailed work.
• Warm, earthy tones complement natural settings. | • Less durable; erodes faster in harsh climates.
• Can stain if not sealed properly. | ### Recommendation If you’re looking for longevity and low maintenance, **granite** is usually the safest bet—especially for high‑traffic gardens or areas exposed to extreme weather. If you prefer a softer, more traditional look and plan to protect it with a sealant, **marble** offers a classic elegance. For a budget option that still looks great, consider **limestone**, but remember to apply a protective sealant to mitigate staining and erosion.
